gaps.question: How to prove the full chain rule when the inner increment vanishes?
gaps.reason: P10–P13 reconstruction: fixed base values plus h/k changes recover every original increment. The quotient split is explicitly conditional on k!=0. P11 defines r(k) by the derivative error for nonzero k and r(0)=0, so multiplying by k gives an exact identity also valid at zero. P12 explicitly states the finite-product limit law; k/h tends to finite g'(t0), so k=h(k/h) tends to zero. The remainder tends to zero along nonzero k and is zero at zero k. Substitution followed by division by h only yields the chain derivative. Constant g=5 demonstrates the excluded division would be0/0 while the repaired formula gives0. This closes D004-G01 without secretly assuming nonzero inner derivative.
